1.title: Google Cloud Data Management Products
1.text: Welcome to Module four: Google Cloud Data Management Products. It covers the exam area two. Exploring data transformation with Google Cloud. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. two point two Determine which Google Cloud data management products are applicable to different business use cases: Cloud Storage, Spanner, Cloud sequel, Alloy D B, Big table, Big Query, Firestore. Relational, non-relational, object storage, sequel and No sequel. Cloud Storage classes including Autoclass. Migrating and modernizing databases. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: two. Exploring data transformation with Google Cloud (about eighteen percent). Exam format: ninety minutes and fifty to sixty multiple-choice questions. Validated against: the official Google Cloud Digital Leader exam guide.

1.title: Key concepts
1.text: Key concepts. Relational. Data in tables with relationships, queried with sequel. Non-relational (No sequel). Flexible data models (documents, key-value, wide-column) that scale horizontally. Object storage. Files stored as objects with metadata, not in tables. sequel. Structured query language for relational data.

1.title: Choosing the product
1.text: Choosing the product. The figure shows this: Which Google Cloud data product fits which need.

1.title: Choosing the product, continued
1.text: Choosing the product. Cloud Storage. What it is: Object storage, highly durable, unlimited scale. Best for: Files, images, video, backups, data lakes. Cloud sequel. What it is: Managed relational database (My sequel, Postgre sequel, sequel Server). Best for: Standard business applications with regional scale. Alloy D B for Postgre sequel. What it is: Postgre sequel-compatible, high-performance managed database. Best for: Demanding transactional and analytic workloads that want Postgre sequel.

1.title: Choosing the product, continued
1.text: Choosing the product. Spanner. What it is: Globally distributed relational database with strong consistency and horizontal scale. Best for: Global applications that need relational integrity at huge scale. Big table. What it is: Wide-column No sequel, very low latency, massive throughput. Best for: I O T, time series, ad tech, large-scale analytics reads and writes.

1.title: Choosing the product, continued
1.text: Choosing the product. Big Query. What it is: Serverless, managed data warehouse and analytics engine. Best for: Analytics on huge datasets with sequel, also across clouds. Firestore. What it is: Serverless document No sequel database. Best for: Mobile and web apps, real-time sync. Exam tip: Files to Cloud Storage. Standard app database to Cloud sequel. Global scale relational to Spanner. Massive low-latency No sequel to Big table. Analytics warehouse to Big Query. App documents to Firestore.

1.title: BigQuery in a few lines
1.text: Big Query in a few lines. Serverless. No servers to manage; Google handles scale. Managed. Storage and compute are separate, so each scales on its own. sequel. Analysts use standard sequel. Multicloud. Big Query Omni analyzes data in other clouds without moving it. Built-in A I. Big Query M L builds models with sequel (Module seven).

1.title: Cloud Storage classes
1.text: Cloud Storage classes. Standard. Access pattern: Frequent access. Typical use: Active data, websites, analytics. Nearline. Access pattern: About once a month. Typical use: Backups read now and then. Coldline. Access pattern: About once a quarter. Typical use: Disaster recovery copies. Archive. Access pattern: Less than once a year. Typical use: Long-term archives, compliance. Autoclass. Access pattern: Moves objects automatically between classes by how they are accessed. Typical use: When access is unpredictable. Colder classes cost less to store but more to access, and have minimum storage durations. Exam tip: Colder equals cheaper to keep, costlier to read. Autoclass picks the class for you.

1.title: Migrating and modernizing databases
1.text: Migrating and modernizing databases. Lift and shift. Move the database as it is to a managed service or a virtual machine. Move to a managed database. For example to Cloud sequel or Alloy D B, so Google runs patching and backups. Modernize. Change to a cloud-native database (Spanner, Big table, Firestore) for scale and new features. Database Migration Service. A managed service that moves databases to Google Cloud with little downtime. Exam tip: Match the product to the data shape: files equals Cloud Storage, tables with joins equals Cloud sequel, Alloy D B or Spanner, huge key-value or time series equals Big table, documents equals Firestore, analytics equals Big Query.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A media company needs to store millions of videos and images at any scale. Which product fits best? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Cloud Storage for object data. Cloud Storage is object storage for files such as videos and images.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A global payment application needs relational data with strong consistency across several continents. Which product fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Spanner, a globally distributed relational database. Spanner is a globally distributed relational database with strong consistency.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. An I O T company must write millions of sensor readings per second with very low latency. Which product fits best? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Big table, a low-latency wide-column No sequel database. Big table gives very low latency and massive throughput for time-series and I O T data.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. An analytics team wants to run sequel on petabytes of data without managing servers. Which product fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Big Query, a serverless data warehouse. Big Query is a serverless data warehouse for large-scale sequel analytics.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. A company stores backup data that it reads about once a quarter and wants low storage cost. Which Cloud Storage class fits best? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Coldline, for data read about once a quarter. Coldline fits data accessed about once a quarter; Nearline is monthly and Archive is yearly or less.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. A company's data access is unpredictable and it wants Google Cloud to choose the storage class by itself. Which feature helps? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Autoclass, which moves objects between classes. Autoclass moves objects automatically between storage classes based on how they are accessed.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Which product is object storage? Answer: Cloud Storage. Question two. Which product is a serverless data warehouse? Answer: Big Query. Question three. Which database is globally distributed and relational? Answer: Spanner.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Which database is a wide-column No sequel for I O T? Answer: Big table. Question five. What are the four storage classes? Answer: Standard, Nearline, Coldline, Archive. Question six. Which service moves databases with little downtime? Answer: Database Migration Service.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Products: Cloud Storage (objects), Cloud sequel, Alloy D B, Spanner (global), Big table (No sequel scale), Big Query (warehouse), Firestore (documents). Big Query: serverless, sequel, Omni for other clouds. Classes: Standard, Nearline (monthly), Coldline (quarterly), Archive (yearly), Autoclass. Migration: lift and shift, managed database, modernize; Database Migration Service.
